newsitem.title: USA: Ford, UAW bargainers work on major issues.
newsitem.headline: Ford, UAW bargainers work on major issues.

text.p: Bargainers for Ford Motor Co and the United Auto Workers union met in subcommittees on Thursday to negotiate over the biggest and most difficult labor contract issues, a Ford spokesman said.
"They're tackling all issues in smaller groups. They're getting to the issues that are at the heart of the talks, including sourcing," said Ford spokesman Jon Harmon.

On Tuesday, UAW President Stephen Yokich selected Ford as the lead company in the union's triennial contract talks with the Big Three U.S. automakers, although talks at General Motors Corp and Chrysler Corp have not been suspended.
Contracts covering more than 385,000 UAW hourly workers at the three companies expire September 14, but Yokich has downplayed the possibility of a strike.
Harmon said the bargainers have made substantial progress "on the issues that are easily settled."
However, he said the talks have not yet progressed to the point where negotiators are meeting late into the night. They ended their meetings at the end of the business day Thursday.
